question:
DRAG DROP -
An engineer must configure remote authentication on a Cisco UCS system. The user password must be encrypted before it is sent to the authentication server.
The company security policy requires the server to be based on an open standard. Drag and drop the UCS CLI AAA configuration commands from the left into the order in which they must be implemented on the right. Not all commands are used.
explanation: RADIUS is an IETF open standard, while TACACS+ is Cisco-proprietary, so RADIUS (not "scope tacacs+") must be used. Source PDF rendering of the official answer boxes was corrupted for this question; order reconstructed from Cisco UCS CLI AAA configuration syntax (scope security > scope radius > create server > set key > commit-buffer).
theory: Cisco UCS Manager's CLI uses a strict scope hierarchy for AAA configuration: scope security enters the security context, scope radius narrows into RADIUS settings, create server <ip> adds a server entry, set key defines the shared secret used to encrypt the password sent to that server, and commit-buffer commits the pending transaction. RADIUS (rather than TACACS+) is chosen here specifically because RADIUS is defined by an open IETF standard (RFC 2865), satisfying the stated 'open standard' requirement, whereas TACACS+ is Cisco-proprietary. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18/19 - AAA protocol comparison and UCS CLI scope hierarchy)
